source_title: Entertainment Ajay Devgn Moves Bombay HC Over FDA Notice On Vimal Elaichi Ads, Hearing On November 4
source_excerpt:
Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn has approached the Bombay High Court to challenge a show-cause notice issued by Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over his appearance in advertisements for Vimal Elaichi. His petition argues that the notice was issued arbitrarily against him as an actor instead of being directed at the manufacturing company.
A division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna is likely to hear the matter on November 4.
ALSO READ: Diljit Dosanjh Addresses 'Satluj' Criticism At Delhi Concert, Says 'We Fought For That Film'
The FDA issued the notice to Devgn, alleging that the Vimal Elaichi advertisements amounted to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product banned in Maharashtra.
The department also issued similar notices to actors Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff, who featured in the campaign.
The FDA had earlier maintained that the Vimal Elaichi campaign indirectly promoted prohibited pan masala products. It also alleged that the brand was linked to the sale of gutkha and pan masala, both banned in the state.
Mumbai, Maharashtra: On notices being issued to actors Ajay Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff over a Vimal Elaichi advertisement, FDA Chief Tukaram Mundhe says, "The hearing before the Assistant Commissioner has been completed, and she will file adjudication proceedings before the Joint Commissioner by next week at the latest. The proceedings will then begin. However, one of the individuals, Ajay Devgn, has approached the Bombay High Court. That is fine, but we are proceeding with our action..."
ALSO READ: Nora Fatehi Summoned As Prosecution Witness In Rs 200 Cr Sukesh Chandrashekhar Fraud Case
Earlier on October 30, FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said proceedings against Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff over alleged violations of state rules had been completed.
According to Mundhe, the department had concluded its investigation and found violations by the actors. He added that the matter would be referred for adjudication the following week.
Although Devgn has challenged the notice in the High Court, the FDA will continue its proceedings before the joint commissioner, Mundhe said.
Ajay Devgn challenged a show-cause notice from Maharashtra's FDA. He argues the notice was arbitrarily issued against him as an actor instead of the manufacturing company.
The FDA alleges that the Vimal Elaichi advertisements amount to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala. This pan masala is a chewable product banned in Maharashtra.
Actors Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff also received similar notices from the FDA. They featured in the same Vimal Elaichi advertising campaign.
The FDA has completed its proceedings and found violations by the actors. The matter is set to be referred for adjudication soon.

बॉलीवुड अभिनेता अजय देवगन ने महाराष्ट्र खाद्य एवं औषधि प्रशासन (FDA) द्वारा विमल इलायची के विज्ञापनों में उनके दिखने को लेकर जारी किए गए कारण बताओ नोटिस को चुनौती देते हुए बॉम्बे हाईकोर्ट का रुख किया है। रिपोर्ट्स के अनुसार, इस मामले की सुनवाई 4 नवंबर को होने की संभावना है।

## FDA नोटिस की पृष्ठभूमि

FDA ने अभिनेता अजय देवगन के साथ-साथ शाह रुख खान और टाइगर श्रॉफ को भी नोटिस जारी किया था, जिन्होंने इसी विज्ञापन अभियान में काम किया था। विनियामक निकाय के अनुसार, विमल इलायची के विज्ञापन कथित तौर पर विमल पान मसाला का सरोगेट प्रमोशन (अप्रत्यक्ष प्रचार) थे, जो महाराष्ट्र राज्य में प्रतिबंधित एक चबाने योग्य उत्पाद है। विभाग का तर्क है कि इस अभियान ने प्रतिबंधित पान मसाला उत्पादों को अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से बढ़ावा दिया।

## कानूनी रुख और चल रही कार्यवाही

* **अभिनेता की याचिका:** अजय देवगन की याचिका में तर्क दिया गया है कि यह नोटिस विनिर्माण कंपनी को लक्षित करने के बजाय एक अभिनेता के रूप में उनके खिलाफ मनमाने ढंग से जारी किया गया था।
* **FDA का पक्ष:** FDA आयुक्त तुकाराम मुंडे ने कहा कि अभिनेताओं के खिलाफ विभाग की जांच 30 अक्टूबर को पूरी हो गई थी और निष्कर्षों में नियमों के उल्लंघन का पता चला। हालांकि देवगन ने हाईकोर्ट का रुख किया है, लेकिन FDA ने कहा है कि वह संयुक्त आयुक्त के समक्ष अपनी कार्यवाही जारी रखेगा।

## कैसे सत्यापित करें

पाठक प्रकाशित होने पर प्रासंगिक केस नंबरों का उपयोग करके बॉम्बे हाईकोर्ट के पोर्टल के माध्यम से आधिकारिक कानूनी filings की पुष्टि कर सकते हैं, या विनियामक अनुपालन और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य नोटिस के संबंध में महाराष्ट्र FDA द्वारा सीधे जारी आधिकारिक घोषणाओं को ट्रैक कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn has approached the Bombay High Court to challenge a show-cause notice issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) concerning his appearance in advertisements for Vimal Elaichi. According to reports, a division bench is expected to hear the matter on November 4.

## Background of the FDA Notice

The FDA previously issued notices to Ajay Devgn, along with fellow actors Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff, who also featured in the advertising campaign. According to the regulatory body, the Vimal Elaichi advertisements allegedly constituted surrogate promotion for Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product that is banned in the state of Maharashtra. The department maintained that the campaign indirectly promoted prohibited pan masala products and was linked to items banned under state regulations.

## Legal Stance and Ongoing Proceedings

* **Actor's Petition:** Ajay Devgn's legal challenge argues that the notice was issued arbitrarily against him as an actor rather than targeting the manufacturing company directly.
* **FDA Position:** FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe stated that department investigations regarding the actors concluded on October 30, and the findings indicated violations. While Devgn has moved the High Court, the FDA has indicated that it will proceed with adjudication proceedings before the Joint Commissioner.

## How to Verify

Readers can verify official legal filings through the Bombay High Court portal using relevant case numbers when published, or track official announcements released directly by the Maharashtra FDA regarding regulatory compliance and public health notices.
